Ensemble projections of range shifts

geo-shift-ensemble.Rd

Climate projections differ between climate models (GCMs), emission scenarios (SSPs) and, on mountains, the lapse rate used to bring coarse climate down to the terrain. A single projection hides this uncertainty. These functions run a range-shift model over every member of an ensemble and report the results as probabilities:

  • geo_climate_scenarios() builds the ensemble of climates on a fine DEM: for each GCM, SSP and lapse rate, the baseline CHELSA climate is downscaled with geo_downscale_lapse() and the change projected by the GCM (future minus baseline, the delta method) is added, so every member shares the observed baseline.

  • geo_shift_ensemble() predicts suitability for the present and every member with a niche model (such as sdm_integrated()), simulates colonisation and extinction with geo_shift_simulate(), and also reports the unlimited-dispersal range (all habitat with suitability at or above the starting threshold) for comparison.

  • summary() gives, per scenario and dispersal assumption, the median and range of the change in range area across members, and the probability that the range shrinks by more than set thresholds.

Usage

geo_climate_scenarios(
  area,
  dem,
  variables = "bio1",
  period = "2071-2100",
  gcm = c("mpi-esm1-2-hr", "ukesm1-0-ll"),
  ssp = c("ssp126", "ssp585"),
  lapse_rates = 5,
  temperature = grep("^bio([1-9]|1[01])$", variables, value = TRUE),
  reader = geo_chelsa_area
)

geo_shift_ensemble(
  model,
  scenarios,
  initial = 0.5,
  dispersal_mean,
  steps = 10,
  nsim = 50,
  seed = NULL,
  elevation = NULL,
  rescale = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'tmr_shift_ensemble'
summary(object, loss = c(30, 50, 80), ...)

Arguments

area, dem

Area to read and fine elevation SpatRaster (metres).

variables

CHELSA temperature variables to downscale (e.g. "bio1", "bio5"); others (e.g. "bio12") are only resampled.

period

Future period (see geo_chelsa_area()).

gcm, ssp

GCMs and scenarios.

lapse_rates

Lapse rates (degrees C per km) to try.

temperature

Which of variables are temperatures (downscaled with the lapse rate); default bio1 to bio11 (the temperature variables).

reader

Function used to read CHELSA (for testing).

model

A niche model with a predict() method returning the probability of presence for a SpatRaster of covariates (such as sdm_integrated()), or a function taking a SpatRaster and returning one of suitability (0 to 1).

scenarios

Result of geo_climate_scenarios(), or a list with current (one SpatRaster, or one per lapse rate) and members (a named list of SpatRasters) and optionally design.

initial

Initial occupancy, as in geo_shift_simulate(); by default the present suitability above 0.5.

dispersal_mean, steps, nsim, seed, ...

Passed to geo_shift_simulate(); steps is the number of dispersal generations between the present and the future period.

elevation

Optional elevation SpatRaster for range edges.

rescale

Divide suitability by its maximum under the present climate (of that lapse rate), so the best present habitat is 1? Niche models give the probability of presence in a plot of some size, which is rarely close to 1; the simulation treats suitability as the per-generation persistence, so unscaled probabilities make most populations die out. Default TRUE.

object

A geo_shift_ensemble() result.

loss

Range-loss thresholds (%) for the probabilities.

Value

geo_climate_scenarios(): a named list with current (a SpatRaster per lapse rate, in list current) and members, a named list of SpatRasters, one per GCM x SSP x lapse rate, with layers named after variables; and a tibble design of the members.

geo_shift_ensemble(): an object of class tmr_shift_ensemble with results, a tibble with one row per member and dispersal assumption ("limited", "unlimited"): member, gcm, ssp, lapse_rate, dispersal, area_now, area_future, change (%) and, with elevation, the shift of the lower edge, median and upper edge (m); and occupancy, the future occupancy (or suitability) rasters.

summary(): a tibble per ssp (if known) and dispersal: number of members, median, minimum and maximum change (%), and p_loss_<x>, the share of members losing more than x% of the range.

See also

geo_shift_simulate(), sdm_integrated(), geo_chelsa_area().
